title: Encrypted Skills Can Become New Security Exploits If AI Agents Know How to Decipher
title_zh: 如果 AI 智能体懂得如何解密，加密技能可能成为新的安全漏洞

paragraphs.en: AI智能体如果能解密，加密技能可能成为新的安全漏洞。 Third-party skills can expose LLM agents to malicious instructions hidden by encoding. We introduce Ciphered Skill Injection (CSI), which embeds such instructions in skill files for agents to decode and follow. We evaluate Caesar and layered variants across eight models and 139 injection-task pairs, separating instruction recovery from attack success. In the primary setting with shortened skills, the variants achieve attack success rates of up to 47.5% and 40.3%, respectively. Successful decoding does not guarantee attack success, and layering has model-dependent effects. The tested skill scanners rarely flag injected skills. These findings highlight the risk of promoting decoded, untrusted content into actionable instructions.
paragraphs.zh: 如果AI智能体能够解密，加密技能可能会成为新的安全漏洞。第三方技能可能使大型语言模型智能体暴露在被编码隐藏的恶意指令中。 我们提出了“加密技能注入”（CSI）方法，该方法将此类指令嵌入技能文件中，供智能体解码并执行。 我们在八种模型和139个注入任务组合上评估了凯撒密码及其分层变体，并将指令恢复与攻击成功区分开来。 在缩短技能长度的主要测试场景中，这些变体的攻击成功率分别高达47.5%和40.3%。 成功解码并不保证攻击成功，且分层效果因模型而异。 经过测试的技能扫描器很少会标记出被注入的技能。 这些发现凸显了将已解码的不可信内容转化为可执行指令所存在的风险。
